$comment: Every project-specific rule lives here. The hook scripts are the engine and
should not need editing. Start by DELETING the rules that do not apply to
you -- a guard that fires on correct code gets the whole set disabled.
Rule of thumb for what belongs here: an action whose damage is not visible
in the diff. If a reviewer would catch it, a linter should catch it, not a

blast_radius.$comment: bash_rules BLOCK (exit 2). Reserve for irreversible actions, or ones that destroy signal.

bash_rules.name: regenerate committed types from the remote schema
bash_rules.message:
Overwrites the generated types file wholesale. A failed or partial generation clobbers it and breaks compilation repo-wide.
  Generate against LOCAL into a temp file, diff it, then move it into place.

bash_rules.name: push schema to the linked remote project
bash_rules.message:
Writes migrations to the LINKED (production) project. There is no rollback.
  If merging already auto-applies migrations, a manual push risks diverging prod from the repo.

bash_rules.name: reset the REMOTE database
bash_rules.message:
Resets the REMOTE database -- destroys production data.
  A bare local reset is fine and is not blocked.

bash_rules.name: re-baseline visual snapshots
bash_rules.message:
Accepts whatever the app currently renders as the new truth. If the diff was a real regression, this silently erases the evidence.
  Look at the failing diff images first.

bash_rules.name: rewrite a quality baseline
bash_rules.message:
Overwrites the committed baseline that the CI gate ratchets against, so a regression becomes the new floor.
  Fix the regression, or re-baseline deliberately as its own reviewed commit.

bash_rules.name: hand-authored release commit
bash_rules.message: Release commits are owned by CI, which resolves the version from the branch. Hand-authoring one desyncs the tag, the commit and the changelog.

blast_radius.$comment2: edit_rules are ADVISORY (stderr, exit 0). An Edit call cannot carry an override, so blocking would be a wall with no escape hatch.

edit_rules.name: package.json version field
edit_rules.message: The version field is owned by the release workflow. Hand-editing it desyncs the tag, the release commit and the changelog.

edit_rules.name: coverage thresholds
edit_rules.message: Coverage floors are no-regression release gates. Raise them, never lower them. If a change drops coverage, add tests rather than moving the floor.

edit_rules.name: lint warning ceiling
edit_rules.message: The warning ceiling is a CI gate. Fix the warnings instead of raising it.

config_sync.$comment: Advisory only, always. These name surfaces that must move together -- often including surfaces OUTSIDE the repo, which is exactly why this cannot block.

rules.name: Content-Security-Policy allowlist
rules.message:
The CSP is the runtime allowlist -- the only thing permitting external origins in production.
  If code now talks to a new third-party host (fetch/script/img/iframe), add a matching source here, and vice versa.
  A missing entry fails silently in prod, never in local dev.
rules.$comment: Point `path` at whatever file holds your CSP -- a host config, a headers file, a middleware module.

rules.name: third-party script key
rules.message:
A third-party provider is usually a multi-surface change -- verify all of them:
  1. CSP allowlist (script-src / connect-src / frame-src)
  2. the hosting platform's env vars, in EVERY environment
  3. the provider's own dashboard (secret, allowed domains)
  Shipping the key without the CSP entry is the classic outage.
rules.$comment: List the providers you actually embed. Left generic on purpose: a rule that fires on providers you do not use is noise.

rules.name: env schema
rules.message:
Required env keys usually throw at startup, before anything renders. If you added, renamed or removed one, keep these in sync:
  - .env.example (checked in)
  - the hosting platform's env vars, in EVERY environment
  - every consumer of the old name

rules.name: enum value added without widening its CHECK constraints
rules.message:
Adding an enum value often also requires widening every CHECK constraint that lists the old values, in the SAME migration.
  Otherwise inserts using the new value fail at runtime with a check_violation (Postgres 23514), not at deploy time.

rules.name: component not declared in its manifest
rules.$comment: Generalizes the 'exists on disk, never deployed' bug. Adjust the three fields to your manifest.
rules.message:
This component has no entry in the manifest, so the deploy will NOT include it.
  It works locally and 404s in production -- often surfacing as a confusing CORS error on the preflight, which sends you debugging the wrong thing.

watch_mode.$comment: Blocks test-runner invocations that would hang the tool call. npm_scripts matching is ANCHORED: listing 'test' does not match 'test:e2e'.

runners.name: Vitest
runners.message:
Blocked: this starts Vitest in WATCH mode and will hang the tool call.

"test": "vitest" is watch-by-default and there is no TTY here to quit it.

  npm run test -- <file> --run        single file, one shot
  npm run test -- -t "<name>" --run   by name pattern

The `--` is required. `npm run test --run` does NOT work: npm swallows the
flag, forwards nothing, and vitest starts watch mode anyway.
runners.hang_message:
Blocked: --ui starts the Vitest UI server and will hang the tool call.

There is no TTY here to quit it. The UI is worth using, but it needs a real
terminal -- ask the user to run `npm run test:ui` themselves, or use
`npm run test -- <file> --run` to get the result here instead.

runners.name: Jest
runners.hang_message:
Blocked: `jest --watch` will hang the tool call -- there is no TTY here to quit it.
  Drop the flag, or pass --ci.
